source.verbatim_statement: \(W_{1}(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{f\in\mathrm{Lip}}\int f(\mathrm{d}\mu-\mathrm{d}\nu)\), where the supremum is taken over all 1-Lipschitz functions.

added_lemmas.statement: The extended Wasserstein loss used by GANICE is exactly the conditioning-marginal average of ordinary outcome-space \(W_1\) distances between the two conditional laws at the same state.

source.locator: Definition 1 and the statewise identity immediately after equation (1), arXiv:2605.10206v1, Section 3.1
source.verbatim_statement: Thus, \(\mathrm{eW}_{1}\) is exactly the conditioning-marginal average of ordinary outcome-space Wasserstein distances.

added_lemmas.statement: For continuous conditioning, GANICE Theorems 2 and 3 give upper and lower minimax results that are matched only up to logarithmic and implementation-transfer factors under its statewise causal risk.

source.locator: Theorems 2--3 and the sentence immediately following Theorem 3, arXiv:2605.10206v1, Section 5
source.verbatim_statement: Theorems 2--3 give minimax optimality, up to logarithmic and implementation-transfer factors, under the statewise causal risk \(\mathrm{eW}_{1}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the three published facts used by the proof as explicit cited leaves and wire them into the target's proof spine; the proposition's claim and narrative metadata are unchanged.

proposed.justification: The smooth equal-marginal separation prevents design-averaged conditional transport theory from being mistaken for the weaker marginal-mixture transport problem while recording the valid one-way upper-bound implication.
proposed.gap: TamanoImaizumi2026GANICE Definition 1 and equations (1)--(2) define extended Wasserstein loss as design-averaged statewise \(W_1\); Theorem 2 gives a logarithmically inflated upper bound under an implementation-transfer condition, and Theorem 3 gives the continuous-conditioning lower bound. The proposition shows that its loss can stay positive when the present marginal \(W_1\) is exactly zero.
proposed.consumer: A referee or practitioner comparing GANICE with the known-design marginal reconstruction benchmark can distinguish its nontransferable extended-loss lower bound and continuous-conditioning upper/lower theory from the valid, generally nonsharp convexity-based marginal upper implication.
